title: Against Heresies
author: irenaeus
attributionNote: The attribution is recorded as the edition and the scholarly consensus give it; where the attribution is disputed, the work says so.
description: Irenaeus's refutation of Valentinian and other Gnostic systems, and the earliest surviving argument for a fourfold gospel. His accounts of the systems he opposes are a principal source for them, which is why the work carries both his argument and his opponents' teaching as he reports it.
historicalContext: Written at Lyons by a bishop who had known Polycarp, in a period when Christian communities were defining their canon and rule of faith against competing schools.
availabilityNote: Streamed from the Christian Classics Ethereal Library at read time. The Ante-Nicene Fathers translation, served by the CCEL. The Greek original survives partly, mainly in quotations; the Latin version is not hosted here.
